To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sustainable provision of bioenergy, food, water and other ecosystem services in rural SSA requires: 1) improved cookstoves, 2) anaerobic digestion for energy and nutrient recycling, 3) pyrolysis for nutrient recycling and carbon sequestration, 4) integrated systems of biogas digester, pyrolysis, water harvesting and irrigation, and 5) community participation and empowerment.

(a) sustainable provision of food and energy in SSA requires a shift to sustainable energy technologies; (b) pyrolysis, anaerobic digester, and composting are sustainable technologies that could be implemented at scale in SSA; and (c) the most sustainable technology for energy and nutrient recycling is a combined anaerobic diges ter pyrolysis system, but this requires a large investment in infrastructure and training.
